dont_know.sentence: If you do not know the answer, choose Bilmiyorum.
dont_know.instructions: Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose Bilmiyorum.

chat.confidence_system: You are taking a Turkish multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.
chat.confidence_instruction: Aşağıdaki çoktan seçmeli soruların her birini yanıtlayın. Açıklama yapmadan, her soru için doğru seçeneğin harfini ve cevabınızın doğru olduğundan ne kadar emin olduğunuzu gösteren 0 ile 1 arasında bir güven puanını belirtilen JSON biçiminde birlikte döndürün. Cevabı bilmiyorsanız Bilmiyorum seçeneğini seçin.

plain.instruction: Aşağıdaki çoktan seçmeli soruyu çöz. Yanıtının son satırına yalnızca 'CEVAP: X' yaz (X = {letters}). Cevabı bilmiyorsanız Bilmiyorum seçeneğini seçin.

runs.note: xAI did not answer 31 attempts within the time limit, and the runner sent each such request again. runs.name: REAX 1.3
runs.note: REAX's released REAX 1.3 weights (decisionmodels/REAX-1.3 at fa4bf7e), a decision model of two parts that both score every question; each option's probability is the 50/50 mean of the two parts'. Part G blends CharlieBT/gx31-decider (Gemma line, from tattrongvu/Jeffan-31b-1710) with PelaAI/KnowLine-31B-Gen1 (Gemma-4-31B); part Q blends gurujustin/sn92-gen-p5 (Qwen3.5-27B line, through baselabs/mammoth-1) with vllm-sr/d3-ultra. The model card calls REAX a decentralised lab on Bittensor subnet 92. It ran on our hardware through the maker's engine (the reax13 mode of reaxlabs/reax-engine at ff8f595, its own server, serve.py), both parts in FP8 (block-128) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, text only, one request at a time. Its card lists English only.
runs.parameters_scope: two full models: part G (Gemma 4 31B line, with vision encoder) + part Q (Qwen3.8-27B line, with vision encoder and 255-way readout)
parameters_source: counted from the checkpoint's safetensors, decisionmodels/REAX-1.3@fa4bf7e
runs.access: REAX Engine server (reax13 mode, the maker's release code), self-hosted, FP8

runs.name: Mammoth-1
runs.note: Base Labs' released mammoth-1 weights (baselabs/mammoth-1 at 61cec44), a decision model post-trained from Qwen3.5-27B that also reads images. It ran on our hardware through its model card's loader (qev's DecisionEngine from OneJev at 81ce62f with the checkpoint's serve.patch, as the card's setup.sh installs it) behind our HTTP server (servers/baselabs_server.py), one request at a time. That runtime reads images only through an engine the patch leaves without the attention the model was trained with, so it is not on the Page images tab. The card mentions a trained "I don't know" option, but its answers have no such output, and our questions offer five options. Probabilities rounded to 6 decimals by the model's own loader. They sum to 1 only within that rounding, and the check before its runs allowed for it. Its card lists English only.
runs.parameters_scope: language model with its LM head + 0.46B vision encoder
parameters_source: counted from the checkpoint's safetensors, baselabs/mammoth-1@61cec44
runs.access: Base Labs server (qev, the model card's loader), self-hosted, BF16

runs.name: SubQ Snap 1.1
runs.note: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.
